title: Automated Tensor Scheduling for Hybrid CPU-GPU LLM Inference on Consumer Devices
event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-07-11 on tensor-granularity hybrid CPU-GPU inference for consumer device LLM deployment
problem: LLM weights often exceed GPU memory capacity on consumer devices (laptops/desktops), making offloading necessary. Existing offloading systems use coarse layer-level or expert-level scheduling, overlooking intra-layer tensor heterogeneity. They also use load-unaware policies that don't respond to changing device conditions (thermal throttling, background interference). CPU execution becomes the new bottleneck after PCIe transfer optimization.
mechanism: ATSInfer combines three mechanisms: (1) Asynchronous CPU-GPU scheduling to coordinate storage, data movement, and computation across heterogeneous backends, (2) Static tensor placement to determine GPU residency under memory and switching-cost constraints, (3) Load-aware dynamic transfer adjusting runtime tensor movement based on inference phase and backend load. Uses Zero-Copy on RTX GPUs to enable SM-driven transfers overlapping with Copy Engine.

evidence.claim: Improves prefill throughput by up to 1.94x over llama.cpp
evidence.condition: Same GPU VRAM budget, consumer device platforms

evidence.claim: Improves decode throughput by up to 3.29x over llama.cpp
evidence.condition: Same GPU VRAM budget, consumer device platforms

evidence.claim: Increases average GPU utilization during decode by about 70%
Load-aware rescheduling triggers when deviation exceeds 15% with minimum interval of 5x recent TPOT
evidence.condition: Minimum re-scheduling interval equal to five times recent TPOT, ~9ms overhead

evidence.claim: Evaluated on RTX 3060 (6GB) laptop and RTX 4090 (24GB) desktop platforms
evidence.condition: Laptop: Intel i7-11800H, 32GB DDR4, PCIe Gen4 x16. Desktop: Intel i7-11700, 64GB DDR4, PCIe Gen4 x16

evaluation_context: Implemented by extending llama.cpp with ~15,000 lines of C++ code. Evaluated on two representative consumer platforms: mid-range laptop (RTX 3060 6GB, Intel i7-11800H, 32GB DDR4) and high-performance desktop (RTX 4090 24GB, Intel i7-11700, 64GB DDR4). Models tested: GLM-Z1-9B, Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, GPT-OSS-20B (RTX 3060); Llama3.1-70B, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, GPT-OSS-120B (RTX 4090). Both dense and MoE models.
limitations: Evaluation limited to two NVIDIA GPU platforms (RTX 3060 laptop, RTX 4090 desktop). Thermal wall on laptop causes TPOT fluctuations. No reported performance/power efficiency metrics. No comparison with server-grade hardware or other consumer GPU vendors (AMD, Intel). Implemented via llama.cpp extension - portability to other inference frameworks unclear.
project_relevance: ATSInfer addresses memory interface and data movement for local LLM deployment on consumer devices. Uses PCIe Gen4 x16 bandwidth with two transfer paths (Copy Engine and Zero-Copy SM-driven). Tensor-granularity placement vs. layer/expert-level is the key innovation for memory-constrained devices. Load-aware scheduling responds to consumer device variability (thermal throttling, background interference). However, the paper does not report HBM/HBF bandwidth (uses GDDR on RTX), performance-per-watt, or peak compute utilization. The focus is on data movement optimization (PCIe transfer reduction via tensor placement) not compute acceleration.
